The headache and double vision had resolved by the first visit, while papilledema had resolved completely by the second visit. The dose of acetazolamide was reduced to 250 mg three times and then twice daily to be tapered off completely by the next visit.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 31-year-old woman presented with double vision, mild headache, bilateral abducens palsy, and severe bilateral papilledema. Brain MRI showed signs of increased intracranial pressure (distended optic nerve sheath, flattening of the globe, partially empty sella, narrowing of bilateral transverse sinus) but no cerebral venous sinus thrombosis. Lumbar puncture revealed high CSF opening pressure, elevated protein, low glucose, and lymphocytic pleocytosis. Brucella serology was positive, and CSF culture confirmed growth of Brucella melitensis. She was treated with ceftriaxone, rifampicin, doxycycline, and acetazolamide. Follow-up at 4 and 10 weeks showed resolution of headache, double vision, and papilledema.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with symptoms and signs of increased intracranial pressure and cranial nerve palsy: double vision, mild headache, bilateral abducens palsy, and severe bilateral papilledema.

Brain MRI showed signs of increased intracranial pressure (distended optic nerve sheath, flattening of the globe, partially empty sella, narrowing of bilateral transverse sinus) but ruled out cerebral venous sinus thrombosis.
CSF analysis showed high opening pressure (>50 cm H2O), elevated protein (117.60 mg/dl), low glucose (2 mmol/L), and pleocytosis (188 WBC/mm3 with 88% lymphocytes).
Brucella agglutination test (Rose Bengal) was positive, with serology showing Brucella abortus 2ME of 1:320 and Brucella melitensis 2ME of 1:320.
CSF culture confirmed growth of Brucella melitensis.
Treatment included injectable ceftriaxone, oral rifampicin, doxycycline, and acetazolamide.
Clinical improvement was observed with resolution of headache and double vision by 4 weeks, and complete resolution of papilledema by 10 weeks.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Brain MRI showed no signs of cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (E001).

While MRI and high CSF opening pressure are consistent with IIH, the CSF pleocytosis, elevated protein, low glucose (E003), and positive Brucella serology and culture (E004, E006) strongly point to an infectious etiology, making IIH less likely as the primary diagnosis.

remaining_uncertainties: Specific exposure history to Brucella was not documented.
